No. I. O. D..9.h........
File No................11. 2. 29

(C.I.D.) Office Notes

Foreign Section, C. I. D.
March 11, 1929.

Inquiries made regarding K. S. Park, applicant for a situation in the Police Force, show that he is not the same person as Herbert S. Park who was convicted at the Mixed Court in 1926 for larceny from Messrs Boyes, Basset & Co. Nanking Road. K. S. Park has not registered at the local Japanese Consulate since he came to Shanghai 3 years ago and it therefore liable to prosecution by the Japanese authorities although the latter do not seem inclined to take any action against him.

Park owns a small factory known as the "Star Press, Trouser Presser", at the No. 731 Avenue Foch, French Town. Prior to the establishment of the latter factory early in 1928, Park was employed as a commercial agent dealing in Korean and Japanese goods. He is not known to have any political leanings, nor is there anything known against his general character.

H.S. King

A/ D. C. I.

Applicant has no special qualifications
in spite of the high salary he asks

H. Robertson
D.I. 11/3/29

JRS

（刑事侦缉处）办公笔记

刑事侦缉处外籍科
1929年3月11日。

经对申请警队职位的 K. S. Park 进行调查，结果显示他并非 Herbert S. Park，后者曾于1926年在会审公廨因盗窃南京路 Boyes, Basset & Co. 商行财物而被定罪。K. S. Park 自三年前抵沪以来，未在当地日本领事馆登记，因此依律应受日本当局起诉，尽管后者似乎无意对他采取任何行动。

Park 在法租界霞飞路731号拥有一家名为“Star Press, Trouser Presser”的小型工厂。在该工厂于1928年初成立之前，Park 受雇为商业代理，经营朝鲜和日本商品。据知他没有任何政治倾向，其一般品行亦无不良记录。

H.S. King

代理副督察长

尽管申请人索要高薪，但并无特殊资历

H. Robertson
侦探督察 1929年3月11日

JRS

SHANGHAI, CHINA.

CABLE ADDRESS
PARKANDCO-SHANGHAI

CODES
A.B.C. 5TH ED. BENTLEY'S
PRIVATE

February 27th, 1929.

R. G. Givens, Esq.
Present.

Dear Sir,

I am a Korean, age 37, possessing a fairly good knowledge of office routines, and can read, write and speak Chinese & Japanese.

Last Spring when Mr. Armstrong was in office, I applied to him for a position as a translator, and I passed examinations in translation and typing, and proved to be satisfactory, I believe, but Mr. Armstrong asked for a paper from the local Japanese Consulate, recognizing me as a registered Korean, so I was not fortunate enough to get the job. Later I heard from Mr. Wright of Thomas that Mr. Armstrong was going away, I called on Mr. Givens again, who then told me to call again in a week's time. By then I was offered a job by an American citizen, and I worked for him till the November last.

At present I am engaged in a small manufacturing enterprise of my own, for which I have men to look after, and I am looking for a position, and I beg to apply to you for a situation in your office as a translator (Chinese & Japanese into English). The salary I require is Tls. 150.

Hoping this application shall meet with your favorable consideration.

I am, Dear Sir,
Yours cordially,
K.S. Park

A.C. (fol)
? Res

P.S. From March 1st.
My address will be at
781. Avenue Foch.

A.B.C. 第五版 BENTLEY'S
PRIVATE

1929年2月27日。

R. G. Givens 先生
台鉴。

尊敬的先生：

我是朝鲜人，现年37岁，具备相当好的办公室常规工作知识，能读、写、说中文和日文。

去年春天 Armstrong 先生在任时，我曾向他申请翻译一职，并通过了翻译和打字考试，我相信表现令人满意，但 Armstrong 先生要求出具当地日本领事馆的文件，以证明我是已登记的朝鲜人，因此我未能有幸获得该职位。后来我从 Thomas 公司的 Wright 先生处得知 Armstrong 先生即将离职，我便再次拜访 Givens 先生，他当时让我一周后再来。届时我已受聘于一位美国公民，并为其工作至去年十一月。

目前我经营着自己的小型制造企业，手下有人打理，我正在寻找职位，特此向您申请贵处翻译一职（将中文和日文译为英文）。我所要求的薪资为规元银150两。

恳请惠予考虑此申请。

尊敬的先生，
您诚挚的，
K.S. Park

A.C. (fol)
? Res

附言：自3月1日起。
我的地址将变更为
霞飞路781号。
